doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Marching band colonization and a possible doctorate
summary: He considers a doctorate on brass band traditions spread by colonization, with only the US evolving jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Right. I’m thinking very seriously about if I do a doctorate to do it based off of the tuba coming out of all these traditions and how slavery, you know, I did a piece once on a talk at Jazz at Lincoln Center about marching band, what’s it called when countries go into another country and they take the — colonization.

You know what I mean? And how colonization, all those European countries that colonized brought their marching band to those countries, whether it’s India, whether it’s the Philippines, whether it’s down in Guiana, whether it’s the United States. And then we took those marching band instruments and played what our folk, what we consider to be our traditional folk music with it, all those different countries. So you’ve got brass band traditions all around the world.

And the only one that evolved into jazz was into the United States. Check it out. I mean it’s pretty amazing. It’s pretty amazing if you think about it. It sounds like massive work to do. I don’t have time.
You get two Ph.Ds for that.
I’m telling you man, I’m telling you.
